## jig v0.2.0-alpha.2

Names become verifiable claims, and the handshake is bound to the TLS session. Nameservers
sign attestations as COSE and bind every proof of control to its action; servers and clients
verify names against per-suffix delegations, and the CLI pins them. Servers sign a
hash-chained record for every block they accept, and clients check it. Identity keys are
encrypted at rest.

This is an alpha. Pre-1.0 releases make no wire, receipt or storage compatibility guarantee, and
jig has not had an external security audit yet (D27).

### Breaking changes

- **The handshake is bound to the TLS session (#234).** The welcome is now
  `jig-handshake-welcome-v2` and signs a `server_nonce` and the connection's TLS exporter
  (RFC 9266), which the client checks against its own. alpha.1 and alpha.2 clients and servers
  cannot complete a handshake with each other. **jig-server must terminate TLS itself**: behind
  a proxy that terminates TLS, the server signs an empty exporter and every remote client
  refuses it. Anything in front of jig-server must pass TLS through (TCP or SNI passthrough).
  `[tls] enabled = false` remains for loopback and local testing only.
- **Federation peers prove their DID (#234).** A server that dials a peer names its own DID in
  `hello` and ends the handshake with a signed `peer_proof` over the transcript and the TLS
  exporter; without one the dialed server closes the connection (4001). alpha.1 servers cannot
  federate with alpha.2 servers.
- **jig-server parses its config strictly (#199).** Every table refuses unknown keys, and a key
  jig-server used to accept fails with a message saying to delete it. **A config copied from
  v0.2.0-alpha.1's `deploy/config.example.toml`, or written by v0.1.0-alpha.1's installer,
  fails to boot until its `[debug] admin_endpoints = false` line is deleted.**
  `dangerously_enable_v0_0_1_rest`, `[execution] pricing_enabled`, `[execution] cost_per_fuel`
  and `[storage]` are refused the same way.
- **The nameserver parses its config strictly (#247).** Unknown keys are refused, and these
  removed sections and keys stop it from starting with a message saying to delete them:
  `[pow]`, `[rate_limits]` (use `[alias_rate_limits]`), `[transparency]`, `[runtime]`,
  `[anomaly_detection]`, `[hot]`, `[federation]`, `storage.backend`, `storage.backend_config`,
  `analytics.backend` and `analytics.backend_config`. Removed `JIG_NS_*` environment variables
  (`JIG_NS_SECRET`, `JIG_NS_POW_*`, `JIG_NS_RATE_*`, `JIG_NS_HOT_*`, the transparency, runtime
  and backend variables, and the federation variables below) are ignored with a warning naming
  each one.
- **Nameserver federation is removed (#237).** The `[federation]` section and its variables
  (`JIG_NS_FEDERATION_ENABLED`, `JIG_NS_ALLOW_DOMAINS`, `JIG_NS_DENY_DOMAINS`,
  `JIG_NS_SEED_PEERS`, `JIG_NS_MAX_PEERS`, `JIG_NS_CACHE_TTL`, `JIG_NS_GOSSIP_INTERVAL`,
  `JIG_NS_HANDSHAKE_TIMEOUT`, `JIG_NS_GOSSIP_BATCH_SIZE`) are gone, and `/.well-known/jig-ns`
  no longer publishes `allow_domains`, `deny_domains` or `cache_ttl_secs`.
- **A nameserver serves the suffixes its config names, and no default (#224).**
  `[v0_0_2.nameserver] alias_suffix` is replaced by the required list
  `[[v0_0_2.nameserver.alias_suffixes]]`; a config with neither, or with the old key, does not
  start. A nameserver set up from the deploy quickstart needs `/etc/jig/jig-nameserver.toml`
  naming its suffix (the unit sets `JIG_NS_CONFIG`). A single-label suffix needs
  `single_label_authority = true`. A DID holds one name per suffix: a second registration, or a
  rotation onto a DID that already holds one, gets 409 `DID_HOLDS_NAME`.
- **Alias proofs are bound to their action (#210).** `POST /v1/register` and `/v1/renew` take a
  COSE proof of control that names the action, the nameserver's DID, the alias and the
  challenge; a signature over the bare challenge is refused. An alpha.1 CLI cannot register or
  renew against an alpha.2 nameserver. Attestations are COSE envelopes; responses carry
  `attestation`, `links`, `reachability` and unsigned `did`, `alias` and `valid_until` hints,
  and no longer `profile_ttl_seconds`. Rotation still takes signatures over the challenge from
  both keys.
- **Servers in `nameserver` mode resolve names only through `[identity.delegations]` (#200).**
  Each suffix lists its `authorities` (the nameserver DIDs whose attestations count) and the
  `nameservers` to ask. A name under a suffix with no entry is refused. `trusted_nameservers`
  is no longer used, and the server warns at startup if it is set.
- **The CLI refuses plaintext servers that are not on its own machine (#142).** `jig` talks
  `http://` only to loopback; anything else needs TLS.
- **The CLI verifies names before it acts on them (#214, #215, #225).** `jig ns resolve`,
  `jig dm`, `jig channel add` and `jig channel kick` accept `alias@suffix` only when an
  authority for the suffix vouches for it, and never fall back to an unverified answer. The
  suffix needs a `[naming.delegations]` entry in `cli.toml`, or a DNS-rooted delegation at
  `https://<suffix>/.well-known/jig-ns-delegation`. This build ships no `@jig` authority, so
  `@jig` names need a `[naming.delegations.jig]` entry.
- **Identity keys are sealed at rest, and a headless machine must say how (#177).** `jig`
  seals each key with the OS keychain, a passphrase (`JIG_KEY_PASSPHRASE` or a prompt), or a
  secret (`JIG_KEY_UNLOCK`), and converts raw `.key` files on first load. With no keychain, no
  terminal and no passphrase or secret, it refuses to create or convert a key and exits 78;
  `JIG_KEYS_STORAGE=plaintext` keeps raw keys, with a warning on every load.
- **New channel slugs follow a grammar (#233).** `#` and then 1 to 64 of `[a-z0-9_-]`, starting
  with a letter or digit; anything else is refused with `INVALID_SLUG`. `#dm/`, `#email/` and
  `#jig/` are reserved namespaces. Existing channels keep their slugs.
- **Handshake refusals and ingest records are COSE (#187).** Refusals are
  `jig-handshake-refusal-v2`, which an alpha.1 client cannot verify.

### What's new

- **Verified names.** Servers (#200) and clients (#201) accept an attestation only from an
  authority of the suffix's delegation, inside its validity window, and ask every listed
  nameserver; two answers naming different DIDs refuse the name. Both keep the attestations
  they act on.
- **Name pins.** A verified name's DID is pinned on first use, by `jig trust verify-name`
  (#213) and by `jig dm`, `jig channel add` and `jig channel kick` (#215). A changed DID is
  refused until `jig trust accept-name` moves the pin.
- **Several suffixes per nameserver** (#224), each with its own registration policy (`open` or
  `closed`, minimum length, reserved names, an allowlist), `GET /v1/suffixes`, and
  `jig-nameserver keygen` for making the nameserver key offline.
- **Signed ingest records** (#161). The server signs a hash-chained record (`seq`, `prev`) for
  every block of a channel it holds, orders history by `seq`, and serves the records with
  history, on WebSocket block frames and at `GET /api/v1/channels/{slug}/records`.
- **Clients check the chain** (#169). History, `jig read`, `jig tail` and `jig chat` verify each
  record's signature, `seq`, `prev` and clock against the chain the device pinned. A fork or a
  rewritten record is refused; a gap in history is fetched from the records route, with a
  warning if the server does not serve it.
- **Identity keys and MLS state encrypted at rest** (#177), with XChaCha20-Poly1305 under a
  data key wrapped for the OS keychain, an Argon2id passphrase or a secret.
- **Channel terms and roles** (#233). `channel-create` names the channel's sequencer and its
  co-owners, and owners can assign and unassign an `admin` role with `role-assign` and
  `role-unassign` blocks.
- **Specifications and libraries:** key links (JEP-0012, `jig_core::key_link`, #235), block
  programs (JEP-0011 draft, #186; `jig_core::program`, #244), contract messages
  (`jig_core::contract`, #206) and block ABI conformance vectors (#182). Nothing carries these
  yet.

### Other changes

- **The nameserver needs no secret** (#192), and **publishes the limits it enforces** as
  `policy.alias_rate_limits` (#197).
- **The v0.0.1 `jig.db` store is gone** (#196). jig-server opens only the derived
  `jig_v002.db`. An upgraded box keeps its old `jig.db`, unused; delete it once no backup needs
  it.
- **Stores migrate once at first boot.** Channels are keyed by the CID of their
  `channel-create` block (#211), and the channels table is rebuilt with each channel's
  sequencer (#233). MLS group rows that name no channel are dropped, with a warning.
- **A config that lists `allowed_block_kinds` explicitly** (as alpha.1's
  `deploy/config.example.toml` and `install.sh` wrote it) does not get the new `role-assign`
  and `role-unassign` kinds: add them to the list, or delete the key to use the defaults
  (#233).
- **Backups include the nameserver** (#239): `jig-backup.sh` snapshots `nameserver_v002.db` and
  `nameserver_v002.key`, refuses a snapshot of the alias store without its key, and no longer
  copies `jig.db`.
- **`jig keys rotate` keeps both keys when its outcome is unknown** (#243): after a timeout, a
  dropped connection, a 5xx or an unreadable reply, nothing is deleted and the CLI says to
  check with `jig ns resolve`.
- **Blocks get a smaller Wasm stack** (#179): 512 KiB, so unbounded recursion traps instead
  of aborting the process.
- **The nameserver refuses `ns-attestation` blocks** (#224), and its unused Postgres, Redis,
  Scylla and DuckDB backends and their cargo features are removed (#122).
- **Servers in `nameserver` mode get no built-in `@jig` delegation in this build** (#218): it is
  added only once the project's authority is set, and the server logs a warning.

### Pending (not merged yet; move into the sections above as each lands)

- Breaking, L6: the nameserver stops falling back to `JIG_CONFIG` and `~/.jig/config.toml`.
- Breaking, #254: server and nameserver keys are sealed at rest. Raw server and nameserver
  keyfiles are refused until they are sealed, a bare `jig-server` with no `[keys] unlock`
  refuses to make a key, and `jig-nameserver keygen` needs `--slot`.
- #255 (F1 slices 7 and 8): its body carries release-note text for the naming breaks and the
  OP-08, NS-01, NS-02 and AB-01 rows; fold it in when it merges.
- Breaking, #236: the `#jig/` channel prefix is reserved for the server; an existing channel
  there is moved aside at boot.
- Breaking, #242: a DID spelled any way but its canonical lowercase form is refused in signed
  objects.
- Change, #250 (JEP-0011 limits): a block's effective limits become the lower of its
  manifest's and the operator's, and a block whose declared memory maximum exceeds the
  effective cap is not run.
- #249: block runtime step 6a, the server's switch to the component runtime.
- #248: R1 slice 0, `jig_core::pow`.
- New, #228: `jig init --request-alias`, `jig keys renew` and `jig keys rotate` work under
  any suffix a nameserver serves (from `/v1/suffixes`), including single-label ones such as
  `jig`, and refuse before signing anything unless the nameserver is an authority for the
  suffix.
- New, #231: `jig block new`, `jig block build` and `jig block lint` for writing blocks.
- L3's server and deploy PR: `install.sh` and `deploy/config.example.toml` stop listing
  `allowed_block_kinds`, so new installs get the defaults.

### Known limitations

- **Live gaps are not filled.** A gap in the chain seen on a live stream moves the head on; the
  missing records are not fetched until the next history read (OP-06).
- **Rotation proofs are not bound** to the action, nameserver or alias (AB-01).
- **`@jig` names need configuration.** This build ships no project authority for `@jig`.

### Threat-register entries mitigated

Statuses are as of this release. *Partial* means part of the entry's decision is implemented;
the register says which part.

| Entry | What this release does | Status |
| --- | --- | --- |
| OP-01 Stripped handshake | Federation peers prove their DID with a signed `peer_proof` (mutual handshake) | Partial |
| OP-02 False handshake answers | The welcome is bound to the TLS session by its exporter | Partial |
| OP-06 Omission and reordering | The server signs a hash-chained record per block, and clients check it; live gaps are not filled yet | Partial |
| OP-08 Key substitution | Names' DIDs are pinned on first use; the CLI refuses remote plaintext | Partial |
| NS-01 False or poisoned resolution | Servers and clients accept only attestations an authority of the suffix's delegation signed, inside their validity | Partial |
| NS-02 Equivocation | Resolvers refuse conflicting answers and keep the attestations they act on; there is no log | Partial |
| AB-01 Challenge replay | Register and renew proofs are bound to the action, nameserver and alias; rotate is not | Partial |
| TM-02 Self-asserted timestamps | History is ordered by the sequencer's signed `seq`, not authors' clocks | Partial |
| OP-03 Suite downgrade | The client refuses a restricted channel under a suite the operator can read | Partial |

Still open or accepted in this release, among others: OP-04 (metadata), OP-10 and AB-05 (Sybil
resistance), AB-06 (provable abuse in encrypted channels), and NS-03. The register lists them
all.
